output.subject: Your message about receiving another person's statement
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for contacting us, and for letting us know so promptly. We have received your complaint.

You told us that an envelope addressed to you arrived today but contained a statement belonging to another person, and that you have not opened anything else. You mentioned that you are worried this may mean your own statement was sent to that person instead. You also asked us to explain what we are doing about this, and where you should send the statement you received.

We understand how unsettling it is to think your financial information may have reached someone else, and we're sorry for the worry this has caused. Thank you as well for taking care with the other person's details.

A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days, including on your question about what to do with the statement you received.

Thank you for your patience.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Customer asked where to return the misdirected statement; the draft does not give instructions. Decide whether to add interim handling guidance (e.g., keep it secure, do not forward) or a return method before sending.
Customer fears their own statement went to the other person; confirm what can be said about this once it has been looked into.
The complaint contains the other person's name, account and address; the draft deliberately omits them. Keep them out of the reply.
Consider whether the 10-business-day wait is acceptable here or whether the customer should be contacted sooner, given the possible exposure of their own information.
Customer has not received their own statement, according to their message; decide whether to address a replacement or alternative access.
